Subject: Renewal question — support coverage and cost optimization

Dylan,

We're approaching our renewal for the Dedicated capacity contract and I wanted to surface two things procurement is asking about:

- We have a handful of unused "seats" on our Support plan that we'd like to re-purpose. Is there a way to convert them into credits for faster response or escalation hours?
- Quantime is exploring whether a small uplift to the uptime tier (99.9% -> 99.99%) makes sense if we can get a predictable price and some kind of volume discount for annual commits.

Can you outline what packaging/discount options are available and whether Redwood would support a one-off conversion of unused seats to "priority credits" that we could spend across our incidents/on-call rotations?

Attached is our internal SOW snapshot so you can see current seat counts and committed capacity. Happy to schedule a quick call this week.

Thanks,

Hi Marta — thanks for the clear ask. Short answers up front: yes, we can do a seat->credit conversion (we call it "priority access credits") and we can model an uptime tier uplift with an annual-commit discount.

A couple of clarifying points so we scope the proposal correctly:
- How many support seats would you want to convert?
- Do you expect to use credits primarily for expedited responses (SLA faster response windows) or for proactive engineering time / on-call rotations?
- Target annual committed spend for the Dedicated capacity?

Conceptually: 1 support seat could convert to a defined number of priority credits that are redeemable for shorter response SLAs, escalation engineer hours, or reserved burst capacity. Credits would be consumed at pre-defined rates (we'll share a matrix) and can be limited to a 12-month expiry window.

I'll loop Vanessa and Karthik into a short proposal — Vanessa has run similar seat-swap pilots, Karthik will math out the price bands. If you prefer, we can put a draft amendment (SOW + pricing) into DocuSign once we align on the numbers.

Would Wednesday 7/14 at 10am PT work for a 30-minute sync?

—Dylan

Folks — forwarding Quantime's ask and Dylan's quick notes. Context: Quantime has spare support seats and wants to repurpose them instead of renewing them as-is. They are open to doing a modest annual commit increase if we offer predictable uptime uplift and a simple credits mechanic.

Suggested approach:
- Define a credits unit: e.g., 1 support seat -> 40 priority credits (example).
- Redemption options: 1 credit = 15-minute response acceleration on P2; 8 credits = 1 escalation engineer hour; 2 credits = on-call handover assistance (30 min).
- Expiry: credits valid 12 months from issuance; allow up to 25% of seats to be converted on renewal without re-pricing the Dedicated capacity baseline.
- Pricing levers: small conversion fee (0.6x of 1 seat monthly price for credits issuance) + annual-commit discount tiers.

Karthik — can you model a couple scenarios (Quantime's SOW shows 12 seats, 3 currently unused) and price: (A) no annual commit change (seat-swap only), (B) +12 month additional 15% commit (discount to Priority tier), (C) + annual commit to reach our 10%/15% bands. Include DocuSign amendment + sample SOW language.

Attaching the uptime coverage matrix we typically use.

Subject: Pricing proposal — Quantime priority credits + seat conversion (draft)

Vanessa / team — draft numbers below based on the SOW Dylan attached (Quantime: 12 support seats, 3 unused). All pricing in USD. This is a starting point for commercial discussion with Quantime.

Summary (high level):
- Base support tiers (for reference):
  * Standard: 99.9% uptime, response window P1=4h, P2=8h (no premium credits)
  * Priority: 99.99% uptime, response window P1=1h, P2=2h (priority credits can be used to pre-empt queuing)

Seat-swap / credits mechanics: 
- Conversion rate: 1 seat -> 40 priority credits (credits valid 12 months)
- Redemption: 8 credits -> 1 escalation engineer hour; 1 credit -> 15-minute response acceleration on P2; 2 credits -> priority routing for scheduled on-call handover (30 min)
- Conversion fee: one-time fee equal to 0.6x monthly price of 1 seat (covers operational changes + billing admin)
- Max swap: up to 25% of committed seats per renewal without re-negotiating baseline capacity (Quantime case: 12 seats -> max 3 swap)

Pricing bands (annual commit discounts on Dedicated + Support combined):
- Commit <$50k/yr: no discount (monthly)
- Commit >= $50k/yr: 5% discount on Support line items
- Commit >= $150k/yr: 10% discount
- Commit >= $350k/yr: 15% discount + waived conversion fee (pilot)

Scenario math (Quantime example):
- Current ARR estimate (Dedicated + Support): $180k
- If they convert 3 seats to credits: conversion fee = 3 * 0.6 * seat_monthly_price (let seat_monthly_price = $1,200) => one-time = $2,160; credits issued = 120 credits.
- If they move to Priority uptime and commit for 12 months with +10% discount band (>= $150k): net uplift cost approx +$12,400/yr after discount (ballpark — need exact invoice-level calc).

Next steps:
1) Confirm exact seat_monthly_price from billing (Marissa?) and whether Quantime wants credits applied to incidents vs scheduled rotations (that changes the expected burn rate).
2) Produce amendment + SOW language for DocuSign (I can draft).
3) Offer a 30-day pilot: convert up to 2 seats to credits immediately, measure burn over 60 days, then finalize full conversion.

Linking a draft DocuSign amendment here: https://www.docusign.com/en/documents/template/QTM-amendment-2027

Karthik Iyer
Director, Pricing & Commercial Strategy
Redwood Inference

Thanks, Dylan / Vanessa / Karthik — this is helpful and the mechanics make sense. A couple quick clarifications from our side before we greenlight a pilot:

1) Expiry: credits valid 12 months is fine. Will you allow a one-time 3-month extension on credits (at a small admin fee) if we can demonstrate low burn during Q4?
2) Scope: can credits be used for both unplanned incidents (P1/P2) and scheduled on-call overlap (e.g., augmenting our rotation for major releases)?

If you can confirm the two points, we're happy to run the 2-seat pilot and sign the amendment. Please send updated SOW and DocuSign link and we'll route to procurement.
